title: Adaptive tenant prescaling & hotkey backpressure controller for console ingest
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Replace the existing static ingress buffer with an adaptive per-tenant prescaling controller that proactively allocates ephemeral processing capacity and applies tenant-scoped backpressure when hotkeys are detected. Goals: reduce tail latency for non-hotkey tenants during hotkey storms, bound memory growth for shard operators, and preserve cost predictability while maintaining near-real-time console metrics. Implementation involves a prescaler service that watches tenant-rate signals + upstream partition lag, a lightweight hotkey detector (approx top-K per tenant with expiring counters), and a tenant-rate-aware admission controller that annotates requests with QoS hints for downstream processors.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end ingest pipeline maintains 99th percentile tail latency for non-hotkey tenants within 1.5x baseline under a simulated hotkey storm
Memory usage per shard operator increases by no more than 20% under worst-case hotkey load compared to baseline
No dropped events for tenants with SLA tier >= standard during prescaled bursts (verified by e2e test harness)
Automatic scaling decisions logged and surfaced in console with per-tenant decision traces
Design doc and interface contracts reviewed and approved by Infra and Platform teams
